All 47 tests compiled and ran; 46 pass and 1 fails, revealing a real bug in the code under test.

**Bug found:** `testToLocaleStringInvalidLanguageWithNumericAreaCodeThrows` — `LocaleUtils.toLocale("q_001")` should throw `IllegalArgumentException` (language code `"q"` is not a valid 2-3 letter ISO-639 code) but instead returns a `Locale` silently. This is caused by a missing parenthesis in `LocaleUtils.parseLocale`:

```java
if (isISO639LanguageCode(language) && isISO3166CountryCode(country) || isNumericAreaCode(country)) {
```

Due to operator precedence, this evaluates as `(isISO639LanguageCode(language) && isISO3166CountryCode(country)) || isNumericAreaCode(country)`, so whenever the country segment is a valid UN M.49 numeric area code (e.g. `"001"`), the language validity check is bypassed entirely — any malformed language prefix combined with a numeric area code is accepted. The fix is to parenthesize it as `isISO639LanguageCode(language) && (isISO3166CountryCode(country) || isNumericAreaCode(country))`, matching the correctly-parenthesized sibling check a few lines below for the 3-segment (language_country_variant) case.
